legend: They call him the Seal, not because he swims, but because every case he touches gets closed. Stamped shut.  Sealed. A few miles up the coast from Aqua Badran sprawls Aquarbour, a city so overcrowded that three people can witness a murder and all swear they were looking the other way. Last Tuesday, someone walked into the Aquarbour National Archive and walked out with the Ledger, a book the city's elite would very much prefer remained unread. The Seal took the case for one shawarma sandwich and a cup of Al Ameed coffee. His only lead: the thief left behind two coded sequences, scratched into the marble floor in two parallel rows.
Row a%%ZSMJ0%% contains n%%ZSMJ1%% marks bearing each odd number from 1%%ZSMJ2%% to 2n%%ZSMJ3%%, in some order.
Row b%%ZSMJ4%% contains n%%ZSMJ5%% marks bearing each even number from 1%%ZSMJ6%% to 2n%%ZSMJ7%%, in some order.
choose one of the two rows,
pick an index i%%ZSMJ10%% from 1%%ZSMJ11%% to n−1%%ZSMJ12%%,
swap the marks at positions i%%ZSMJ13%% and i+1%%ZSMJ14%% of that row.
Row a%%ZSMJ15%% was cut into soft limestone, each swap costs ca%%ZSMJ16%% units of effort.
Row b%%ZSMJ17%% was cut into hard Aquarbour granite, each swap costs cb%%ZSMJ18%%.
input: The first line contains t%%ZSMJ25%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ26%%), the number of cases on the Seal's desk. For each test case:
The first line contains three integers n%%ZSMJ27%%, ca%%ZSMJ28%%, cb%%ZSMJ29%% (1≤n≤105%%ZSMJ30%%; 1≤ca,cb≤109%%ZSMJ31%%).
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ32%% integers a1,…,an%%ZSMJ33%%, all odd, pairwise distinct, each between 1%%ZSMJ34%% and 2n%%ZSMJ35%%.
The third line contains n%%ZSMJ36%% integers b1,…,bn%%ZSMJ37%%, all even, pairwise distinct, each between 1%%ZSMJ38%% and 2n%%ZSMJ39%%.
output: For each test case, print one integer, the minimum effort the Seal must spend before the marble gives up its name.
note: Case 1. The marble is already talking (3<4%%ZSMJ42%%). The Seal lights a cigarette and writes the name down. Cost: 0%%ZSMJ43%%. Case 2. Granite is unforgiving (cb=3%%ZSMJ44%%). The Seal works only the limestone row, sliding 1%%ZSMJ45%% to the front of row a%%ZSMJ46%% in two swaps: [1,5,3]%%ZSMJ47%%, which already reads smaller than [2,4,6]%%ZSMJ48%%. Cost: 2⋅1=2%%ZSMJ49%%. Case 3. Now both chisels come out. One swap on row a%%ZSMJ50%% (cost 4%%ZSMJ51%%) brings 5%%ZSMJ52%% to the front: [5,7,3,1]%%ZSMJ53%%. One swap on row b%%ZSMJ54%% (cost 3%%ZSMJ55%%) brings 6%%ZSMJ56%% to the front: [6,2,4,8]%%ZSMJ57%%. Since 5<6%%ZSMJ58%%, the marble confesses. Total cost: 4+3=7%%ZSMJ59%%.
